Two separate ground nodes are drawn and both are named 0 per the rule that all GND symbols share one reference: (i) the bottom rail at y~364-368 running from V-AC 4's bottom stem at x=23 right to I-AC 1's bottom stem at x=491, carrying V-AC 4 bottom, V-AC 7 bottom (stem at x=85), GND 10 (stem at x=170), MOSFET 13 source (x=237), MOSFET 2 source (x=350), I-AC 0 bottom (x=439) and I-AC 1 bottom (x=491); and (ii) the isolated node V-DC 8 right terminal -> right along y=136 to x=380 -> down to GND 11's bar at y=156. Judgment calls: (a) All six MOSFETs are drawn with the same convention, verified at 8-16x: an isolated gate bar with a single lead, and three channel-side leads of which the middle one carries the body arrow and is wired together with the LOWER lead. I therefore read the upper channel lead as drain and the lower (body-tied) lead as source for every transistor, and ordered terminals [drain, gate, source]. MOSFET 6, 3, 12, 13 have the gate on the left and the channel leads on the right; MOSFET 9 and 2 are drawn mirrored (channel leads exit left, gate bar on the right with its lead running right). (b) MOSFET 13: pixel column x=237 shows ink at y=295..306 and again at y=317..367 with a clean 10-px gap, confirming its drain (up, n5) is NOT shorted to its source (down, ground) even though both leads leave on the same side. The same gap test was applied to MOSFET 6 (x=110, gap y=165..171), MOSFET 3, MOSFET 12 (drain leaves at x=229, source at x=236) and MOSFET 9/2 (x=351: runs 240..315 then 323..363). (c) Both crossings on the MOSFET-3-gate column are drawn semicircular hops, not junctions: the column swings from x=146 at y=210 out to x=153 at y=218 and back to x=148 at y=244 (hop over n3), and from x=155 at y=250 out to x=157 at y=257 and back to x=155 at y=262 (hop over n2). Neither carries a dot; the real junctions in this drawing (226,137), (226,214), (237,282), (350,282), (145,283) all show a distinct 4-6 px ink blob. (d) Zener 14 sits in the left rail between the top rail and n2. The bar (with the characteristic zener Z-bends) is the upper element at y~207 and the triangle is below it with its base at y~227, so I read the top lead as the cathode and the bottom lead as the anode; terminal order is top-then-bottom, which does not affect any metric either way. (e) V-DC 8 / GND 11 form a node with no wire to the bottom rail, but the protocol names every GND-touching net 0, so it shares the name with the main rail. Bootstrap values were almost all wrong and were rebuilt from the drawing (e.g. it had MOSFET 2 gate = n11 shared with I-AC 0/1 and MOSFET 13, and left 8 terminals null).
